met_analysis:
The Cyclonic Storm “Akvan” [Pronunciation: Akvan] over central parts of South and adjoining Westcentral Bay of Bengal remained practically stationary during past 03 hours and lies centered at 1730 hours IST of today, the 17th November, 2026 over the same region, near Latitude 12.3°N and Longitude 85.6°E, about 590 km east of Chennai (Tamil Nadu), 630 km northeast of Trincomalee (Sri Lanka), 650 km southeast of Machilipatnam (Andhra Pradesh), 650 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh) and 780 km south of Gopalpur (Odisha). It is very likely to move slowly north-northwestwards and intensify further into a Severe Cyclonic Storm over westcentral Bay of Bengal around morning of tomorrow, the 18th November. Thereafter, it is likely to move northwestwards and intensify further into a Very Severe Cyclonic Storm around evening of 19th November, 2026. Continuing to move northwestwards, it is likely to cross Andhra Pradesh & Yanam coasts between Nellore and Visakhapatnam, around noon of 20th November, 2026 as a very severe cyclonic storm with the maximum sustained wind speed of 120-130 kmph gusting to 145 kmph.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Northeast Assam & neighbourhood extending upto 1.5 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Sikkim & neighbourhood at 3.1 km above mean sea level persists.
